page.$description: A desk. Cards are sheets laid on it, so it has to be a step down from them rather than the almost-white it was, where a card and the page behind it read as one surface.

muted.$description: The weakest type on the screen, and what a skill label is written in. It has to clear 4.5 against the page and not merely against a card.

strong.$description: A rule is structure and outranks a word. At ink.500 it was the same value as text-muted, which is how a section head and the line under it ended up the same weight.

tint.$description: The ground under something selected or hovered. A tint of the accent, pale enough that every text role still clears 4.5 on it.

danger.$description: Destructive UI actions and invalid input. Deliberately not the outcome ramp: a delete button is not a failed roll, and overloading the four degrees of success would move them whenever the chrome changes.

scrim.$description: The ground behind a bottom sheet. It must darken the page in both themes, so no surface role fits: surface-sunken is a pale grey in light.

effect.$description: What an effect is doing to a number, and which way. Separate from accent because accent means "you can interact with this": when a raised shield and a hyperlink were the same teal, a marked armour class read as a link and a link read as a buff. Separate from the outcome ramp because a bonus is not a successful roll.

chrome.$description: The navigation rail and bottom bar. The one place the accent is a ground rather than a mark, so the app has a colour of its own before any content loads.

elevation.$description: Cards are sheets laid on a desk, and a sheet casts a little shadow. Borders still do the separating; this only lifts.
